name: Château-Thierry
summary: Pursuing Sacken and Yorck to the Marne, the Guard cavalry and Ney's infantry caught their rearguards before Château-Thierry and drove them over the river, but the bridge was burnt behind them.

sources.label: Allied and French Forces, Battle of Montmirail, 11 February 1814 (Nafziger Collection 814BAA)
Six Days' Campaign order of battle (Wikipedia)

forces.name: Christiani's Division
forces.summary: The Guard's second division, under Christiani now that Michel had been wounded, which led Mortier's pursuit up the high road towards the Marne and came on head on at the allied rearguard.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
Michel was wounded at Montmirail; Christiani led the division from the next day, as Wikipedia's account has it.

The division had 3,878 men. Nafziger gives it without brigades: the chasseur and grenadier regiments are brigaded here as the list takes them, flanqueurs with fusiliers, and the vélites as its Italian brigade.
The Flanqueurs-Chasseurs and Flanqueurs-Grenadiers, the Young Guard's light infantry, are the list's Tirailleurs.
Nafziger gives the Guard artillery together, seven foot and four horse batteries, not by division; the batteries here are those the list's brigades take.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Meunier's Division
forces.summary: Ney's first Young Guard division, which followed Christiani's up the high road behind the allied rearguard.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
Its regiments were newly raised that winter, largely of conscripts under a cadre of veterans; they are the list's Young Guard, as it rates them.
The division had 4,133 men in eight battalions; they are shown at full size.
Battalion numbers, brigades and guns, which this return leaves out, are as at La Rothière.
Its foot battery, with four battalions in its brigade, where the list wants six for one, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Friant's Old Guard
forces.summary: The Old Guard's first division, which followed the pursuit; two battalions of its Chasseurs à Pied, with Guyot's duty squadrons, fell on Katzler's Prussians at Viffort, and two hundred grenadiers took Petite-Noue.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
The division had 4,796 men in eight battalions. The 1st Chasseurs and Grenadiers à Pied are the list's Old Guard, and the 2nd, raised in 1811, its Middle Guard.
Nafziger gives Michel as the commander of the chasseurs' brigade as well as of the 2nd Old Guard Division; the brigade is shown here without him.
Nafziger gives the Guard artillery together, seven foot and four horse batteries, not by division; the batteries here are those the list's brigades take.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Colbert's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: Ney led the Guard's cavalry after the allied rearguard; Colbert's division rode with Laferrière's and Lefebvre-Desnouettes's against the Prussian columns.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
The division had 2,582 men. Each Guard cavalry regiment had squadrons in each of the three divisions; each division's are shown as one unit of each regiment.
Nafziger gives the division without brigades; its regiments are brigaded here as the list takes them.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lefebvre-Desnouettes's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: With the rest of the Guard's cavalry under Ney in the pursuit to the Marne.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
Its strengths are of 28 January: some 3,300 men, the grenadiers about nine hundred and the other regiments six to seven hundred each.
Nafziger gives the division without brigades; its regiments are brigaded here as the list takes them, the Gendarmes d'Élite as the small unit the chasseurs' brigade may have with it.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Laferrière's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: The division that did most in the pursuit: its Guard dragoons rode at the Prussian columns, and Letort's squadrons broke Horn's brigade before the town and took its guns.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.

Lion's brigade was the chasseurs, about five hundred, and the Empress Dragoons, about seven hundred; Letort's the grenadiers, about eight hundred and fifty. The dragoons are with Letort's grenadiers here, as the list's heavy brigade takes them.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur
forces.formation: Cavalry Division, attached to the Guard
forces.summary: The Gardes d'Honneur, who charged the Prussian columns with Laferrière's dragoons.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
The Gardes d'Honneur, raised in 1813 from young men of means who equipped themselves and rode dressed as hussars, are the list's Hussars.
The division had only 896 men in five regiments; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.

Nafziger gives the division without brigades. Piquet's brigade of the 10th Hussars and the 1st Gardes d'Honneur, and Ségur's of the 3rd and 4th, are as at La Rothière; the 2nd Gardes d'Honneur are with Ségur's here, three hussar regiments where the list's brigade takes two, a historical departure.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Yorck's Corps
forces.summary: Yorck's brigades, covering Sacken's crossing of the Marne. Katzler's advance guard held Montfaucon and Viffort until the Guard drove it in; Horn's brigade, blocking the high road, was broken before the town by Letort's squadrons, and two East Prussian battalions were cut off and taken.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.

Only these two of Yorck's brigades are on Nafziger's return. Its four grenadier battalions, each of a different regiment, are grouped in pairs as regiments, as the list takes them; they have its Veteran upgrade.
The East Prussian National Cavalry, a volunteer regiment, is the list's small Landwehr cavalry regiment, and the Brandenburg Hussars its small hussar regiment, each attached to its brigade.
Each brigade's battalions are shown at full size, though most were well under strength by now.
The 13th Silesian Landwehr's four battalions, where the list's Landwehr regiment takes three, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lieven's Corps
forces.formation: XI Infantry Corps, Sacken's corps, Army of Silesia
forces.summary: Lieven's corps, already beaten at Montmirail, falling back over the Marne at Château-Thierry behind Yorck's rearguard.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
Zass's 10th Division (the first two brigades), Selivanov's brigade of the 16th, and Stavitsky's 27th (the last three).
Its regiments had one or two field battalions each, a few hundred men; each is shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.
The corps' three batteries are with the brigades, as the list takes them.
Four infantry brigades and two Jäger brigades, where the list allows three and one, and three regiments in Sokolovsky's brigade, where it takes two, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 3 of the 6 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Talyzin's Corps
forces.formation: VI Infantry Corps, Sacken's corps, Army of Silesia
forces.summary: Talyzin's corps, falling back over the Marne behind Yorck's rearguard; Heidenreich's brigade, with the Tambov and Kostroma regiments, was overrun and mostly taken.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.

Prince Shcherbatov's 7th Division (the first three brigades) and Bernodessov's 18th (the last three). Nafziger names Talyzin as the corps' commander; Wikipedia's account has Shcherbatov sick and Talyzin acting for him.
Each regiment had a single battalion; each is shown as its one battalion, at full size.
The corps' three batteries are with the brigades, as the list takes them.
Four infantry brigades and two Jäger brigades, where the list allows three and one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 3 of the 6 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Vasilchikov's Cavalry
forces.summary: Sacken's horse, covering the retreat to the Marne; a dragoon regiment was routed by the Guard cavalry.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
Built from Nafziger's order of battle for Montmirail the day before; he has none for Château-Thierry. Who was engaged is from Wikipedia's account of the battle.
Lanskoy's 2nd Hussar Division (the light brigades) and Panchulidzev's 3rd Dragoon Division (the dragoons), with its three horse batteries.

Two light and two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list allows one of each, three horse batteries, where it allows two for eight regiments, and cavalry with no infantry brigade to allow it, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 4 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.
